newsitem.title: USA: U.S. official meets Serbian student protesters.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official meets Serbian student protesters.

text.p: The U.S. State Department's top Europe official met on Wednesday with leaders of Serbian students protesting against President Slobodan Milosevic and said he expressed support for their goals.

"It was important for us to hear their views because it is hard for us to get grass-roots opinion, but secondly because we were able to stress to them our support for what they are doing," Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum said.
Belgrade students have protested alongside the Serbian opposition coalition Zajedno for the past nine weeks against the government's refusal to recognise Zajedno victories in local elections Nov. 17.

The four students who met Kornblum at his State Department office are on a U.S. tour sponsored by Yugoslav-born Milan Panic, who has reverted to his life as a California businessman after serving as Yugoslav Prime Minister in 1992.
Kornblum quoted the students as saying they thought there had been a "true awakening" in their country since the 1995 Dayton agreement which ended the war in neighbouring Bosnia.

"During the war period there had been a certain apathy and people were really trying to survive, but as the Dayton agreement was signed and as sanctions (on Yugoslavia) were lifted and people could focus on the future, there was this awakening," he quoted them as saying.
But the students also told Kornblum they were afraid the Serbian authorities, who have been relatively restrained so far in their handling of the protests, might soon resort to violence.

"They said that they believed that their country was now at a crossroads and that there was a danger of yet another war in Yugoslavia -- this would be a civil war inside Serbia -- or there was the possibility of a democratic development," Kornblum said.
"They urged us and the international community to support the democratic course."

The United States, which has demanded that Milosevic accpet the election results and hand over control of city assemblies, is imposing new sanctions on Belgrade including witholding high-level visits and discouraging trade.
The students who met Kornblum were Daliborka Uljarevic, Dusan Vasiljevic, Dragan Pecinar and Alexa Grgurevic.
